intro: Hi! You know I enjoy swimming, I want to go and I used to live in Bogor. Now meet the verbs that change their meaning with -ing or to (I stopped smoking is not the same as I stopped to smoke!), the difference between used to and I'm used to + -ing, and how to say what you want someone else to do. Warm-up: what is something that was hard for you at first but is normal now?
teachingNotes: Build on b1-gerunds-infinitives (verb + -ing lists like avoid / suggest, verb + to lists like decide / afford, -ing after prepositions, 'look forward to + -ing' as a phrase) and b1-used-to (used to + base form for past habits, didn't use to). Recap each in one line; don't re-teach them. Use A0–B1 grammar only; no third conditional, wish, causative have/get something done, past modals or participle clauses.

Meaning changes: remember / forget + -ing = a memory of a past action; remember / forget + to = a task (forgot to lock = didn't lock). forget + -ing is natural mostly in 'I'll never forget + -ing'. stop + -ing = the activity ends (for good or right now); stop + to = stop in order to do something else (berhenti UNTUK). Common error: *'I stopped to smoke last year' meaning 'I quit' → I stopped smoking last year. regret + -ing (menyesal sudah) vs 'We regret to inform you' (formal) is a note only: don't test regret.

try is partly a tendency: for a failed attempt natives say both 'I tried to call you' and 'I tried calling you', so never mark either wrong there. Only test the clear cases: 'be trying to + verb' (effort, it's hard: *'I'm trying finishing' is wrong) and 'Try + -ing' as advice/an experiment ('Try restarting it'). Always give a context that fixes the meaning (memory vs task, quit vs pause, effort vs experiment).

used to + base form (dulu) vs be used to + -ing / noun (sudah terbiasa) vs get used to + -ing / noun (mulai terbiasa). In be / get used to, 'to' is a preposition, so -ing follows. Common errors: *'I'm used to wake up early' → I'm used to waking up early; *'I used to waking'. Indonesian trap: 'biasa' (habit now = usually + present simple) vs 'terbiasa' (be used to). be / get used to work in any tense (wasn't used to, will get used to, have got used to: British 'got', American 'gotten').

Verb + object + to-infinitive: want / would like / ask (= meminta) / tell (= menyuruh) / expect / need + me, him, her, us, them, Budi + to + base form; negative 'not to' (told me not to worry). Common error: *'She wants that I come' (from 'Dia ingin agar saya datang') → She wants me to come; also *'wants I come', *'wants me come'. Contrast make / let + object + base form WITHOUT to (*'let me to go', *'made me to stay'); allow takes to. Mention that suggest does not take object + to (*'suggested me to go'), but don't drill it.

Don't teach other meaning-change verbs (go on, mean, need + -ing, see/hear someone doing), passive 'be made to', or verb + object + -ing. Keep sentences adult and real (office, kos, KRL, campus, ojek online, doctor).

keyPoints.title: remember, forget, stop, try: -ing or to changes the meaning
keyPoints.explanation: remember / forget + -ing = a memory of something you did (I'll never forget seeing Bromo); remember / forget + to = a task you do (or don't do) after remembering (I forgot to lock the door = I didn't lock it). stop + -ing = the activity ends (stopped smoking = quit); stop + to = stop in order to do something else (stopped to smoke = berhenti untuk merokok). try + to = make an effort, it's hard (I'm trying to sleep); try + -ing = an experiment (Try restarting it). regret to inform you is a formal phrase.

examples.id: Saya ingat pernah bertemu Pak Hasan di sebuah konferensi di Surabaya.

examples.en: My father stopped smoking ten years ago.
examples.id: Ayah saya berhenti merokok sepuluh tahun yang lalu.

examples.id: Sopirnya berhenti di warung untuk merokok.

id.title: remember, forget, stop, try: -ing atau to mengubah makna
id.explanation: remember / forget + -ing = kenangan tentang sesuatu yang sudah kamu lakukan (I'll never forget seeing Bromo); remember / forget + to = tugas yang kamu lakukan (atau tidak kamu lakukan) setelah ingat (I forgot to lock the door = pintunya tidak saya kunci). stop + -ing = kegiatannya berhenti (stopped smoking = berhenti merokok); stop + to = berhenti untuk melakukan hal lain (stopped to smoke = berhenti untuk merokok). try + to = berusaha, karena sulit (I'm trying to sleep); try + -ing = percobaan (Try restarting it). regret to inform you adalah ungkapan formal.

keyPoints.title: used to + verb vs be / get used to + -ing
keyPoints.explanation: used to + base form = a past habit or state that isn't true now (I used to live in Bogor = dulu). be used to + -ing or a noun = it's normal for you now, sudah terbiasa (I'm used to working at night). get used to + -ing or a noun = becoming used to it, mulai terbiasa (You'll get used to living alone). In be / get used to, to is a preposition, so the verb takes -ing: I'm used to waking up early, not 'I'm used to wake up early'. be / get used to work in any tense.

examples.en: I used to work at night, but now I have a day job.
examples.id: Dulu saya kerja malam, tapi sekarang saya kerja siang.

examples.en: I'm used to working at night.
Rina is getting used to her new job in Surabaya.
examples.id: Rina mulai terbiasa dengan pekerjaan barunya di Surabaya.

id.title: used to + kata kerja vs be / get used to + -ing
id.explanation: used to + bentuk dasar = kebiasaan atau keadaan di masa lalu yang sekarang tidak berlaku lagi (I used to live in Bogor = dulu). be used to + -ing atau kata benda = sudah biasa untukmu sekarang, sudah terbiasa (I'm used to working at night). get used to + -ing atau kata benda = proses menjadi terbiasa, mulai terbiasa (You'll get used to living alone). Dalam be / get used to, to adalah preposisi, jadi kata kerjanya pakai -ing: I'm used to waking up early, bukan 'I'm used to wake up early'. be / get used to bisa dipakai di semua tense.

keyPoints.title: verb + object + to: want someone to …
keyPoints.explanation: To say what you want another person to do, use want / would like / ask / tell / expect / need + object (me, him, her, us, them, Budi) + to + base form: She wants me to come, not 'She wants that I come' (the Indonesian 'ingin agar saya datang' trap). Negative: told me not to worry. make and let take the object + base form without to: My boss made me redo the slides; My parents let me study in Yogyakarta. allow takes to: allowed me to study.

examples.en: My boss wants me to lead the meeting.
examples.id: Bos saya ingin saya memimpin rapatnya.

examples.en: The doctor told him not to work this week.
examples.id: Dokter menyuruhnya tidak bekerja minggu ini.

examples.en: My parents let me study in Yogyakarta.
examples.id: Orang tua saya mengizinkan saya kuliah di Yogyakarta.

id.title: kata kerja + objek + to: want someone to …
id.explanation: Untuk mengatakan apa yang kamu ingin orang lain lakukan, pakai want / would like / ask / tell / expect / need + objek (me, him, her, us, them, Budi) + to + bentuk dasar: She wants me to come, bukan 'She wants that I come' (jebakan 'ingin agar saya datang'). Negatif: told me not to worry. make dan let diikuti objek + bentuk dasar tanpa to: My boss made me redo the slides; My parents let me study in Yogyakarta. allow pakai to: allowed me to study.

material.title: remember and forget: a memory or a task?

id.title: remember dan forget: kenangan atau tugas?

blocks.text:
Quick recap from B1: some verbs take **-ing** (*enjoy, avoid*), others take **to + base form** (*want, decide*), and with *like, love, start* both forms mean the same. (The **base form** is the dictionary form: *lock, buy, call*. **to + base form** is also called the **to-infinitive**.)

A few verbs are different: they take both forms, but **the meaning changes**. Start with **remember** and **forget**:
- **remember / forget + -ing** = a **memory**. You did it first; later you remember it (or you will never forget it). The action is in the **past**.
- **remember / forget + to** = a **task**. You remember first, then you do it (or you forget, so you **don't** do it). The action comes **after**.

A trick: **-ing looks back, to looks forward.**

id.text:
Rangkuman singkat dari B1: ada kata kerja yang diikuti **-ing** (*enjoy, avoid*), ada yang diikuti **to + bentuk dasar** (*want, decide*), dan dengan *like, love, start* kedua bentuk artinya sama. (**Bentuk dasar** = bentuk di kamus: *lock, buy, call*. **to + bentuk dasar** juga disebut **to-infinitive**.)

Ada beberapa kata kerja yang berbeda: bisa diikuti kedua bentuk, tapi **artinya berubah**. Kita mulai dengan **remember** (ingat) dan **forget** (lupa):
- **remember / forget + -ing** = **kenangan**. Kamu melakukannya dulu; belakangan kamu mengingatnya (atau tidak akan pernah melupakannya). Tindakannya ada di **masa lalu**.
- **remember / forget + to** = **tugas**. Kamu ingat dulu, lalu melakukannya (atau kamu lupa, jadi **tidak** melakukannya). Tindakannya terjadi **sesudahnya**.

Trik mengingatnya: **-ing melihat ke belakang, to melihat ke depan.**

rows.en: I remember meeting Pak Hasan at a conference in Surabaya.
rows.id: Saya ingat pernah bertemu Pak Hasan di sebuah konferensi di Surabaya.

rows.en: Remember to bring your ID card tomorrow.
rows.note: task: first remember, then bring it

rows.en: I'll never forget seeing Mount Bromo at sunrise.
rows.id: Saya tidak akan pernah lupa saat melihat Gunung Bromo waktu matahari terbit.

rows.en: Budi forgot to send the invoice, so the client didn't pay.
rows.id: Budi lupa mengirim tagihannya, jadi kliennya tidak membayar.

blocks.text:
Indonesian trap: *ingat* and *lupa* don't show the difference, so you have to choose in English.
- *Saya lupa mengunci pintu* usually means you **didn't** lock it: **I forgot to lock the door.** This is the common one.
- **forget + -ing** is used almost only in **I'll never forget + -ing** (a memory you'll keep).
- **remember + -ing** = *ingat pernah / ingat sudah …*: *I remember locking the door* = saya ingat sudah mengunci pintu (so it's locked).

id.text:
Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: *ingat* dan *lupa* tidak menunjukkan bedanya, jadi dalam bahasa Inggris kamu harus memilih.
- *Saya lupa mengunci pintu* biasanya berarti pintunya **tidak** kamu kunci: **I forgot to lock the door.** Inilah yang paling sering dipakai.
- **forget + -ing** hampir hanya dipakai dalam **I'll never forget + -ing** (kenangan yang akan selalu kamu ingat).
- **remember + -ing** = *ingat pernah / ingat sudah …*: *I remember locking the door* = saya ingat sudah mengunci pintu (jadi pintunya terkunci).

blocks.prompt: Sari, your phone battery is at 5%. Remember ___ it before you leave the office.
blocks.explain: Charging the phone is a task for later (remember first, then charge it), so remember + to: remember to charge. 'remember charging' would be a memory of something you already did.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Sari, your phone battery is at 5%. Remember ___ it before you leave the office.
id.explain: Mengisi baterai HP adalah tugas untuk nanti (ingat dulu, baru dicas), jadi remember + to: remember to charge. 'remember charging' berarti kenangan tentang sesuatu yang sudah kamu lakukan.

material.title: stop and try (and a note on regret)

id.title: stop dan try (plus catatan tentang regret)

blocks.text:
**stop + -ing** = the activity **ends**: you don't do it any more (for good, or right now). *My father stopped smoking ten years ago. Stop talking, please.*
**stop + to** = you stop what you're doing **in order to** do something else: *The driver stopped to smoke* = sopirnya berhenti **untuk** merokok (he stopped driving, and then he smoked!).

**try + to** = make an **effort** to do something difficult; maybe you can't do it: *I'm trying to sleep, but the neighbours are very loud.* (berusaha)
**try + -ing** = do something as an **experiment**, to see if it helps or works: *If your laptop is slow, try closing some tabs.* (coba …, lalu lihat hasilnya)

id.text:
**stop + -ing** = kegiatannya **berhenti**: kamu tidak melakukannya lagi (untuk seterusnya, atau saat itu juga). *My father stopped smoking ten years ago. Stop talking, please.*
**stop + to** = kamu berhenti dari apa yang sedang kamu lakukan **supaya bisa** melakukan hal lain: *The driver stopped to smoke* = sopirnya berhenti **untuk** merokok (dia berhenti menyetir, lalu merokok!).

**try + to** = **berusaha** melakukan sesuatu yang sulit; mungkin tidak berhasil: *I'm trying to sleep, but the neighbours are very loud.*
**try + -ing** = melakukan sesuatu sebagai **percobaan**, untuk melihat apakah itu membantu atau berhasil: *If your laptop is slow, try closing some tabs.* (coba …, lalu lihat hasilnya)

rows.en: My father stopped smoking ten years ago.
rows.id: Ayah saya berhenti merokok sepuluh tahun yang lalu.

rows.en: The driver stopped at a warung to smoke.
rows.id: Sopirnya berhenti di warung untuk merokok.
rows.note: stop + to = stop in order to

rows.en: I'm trying to save money for a house.
rows.id: Saya sedang berusaha menabung untuk beli rumah.
rows.note: try + to = make an effort (it's hard)

rows.en: Can't sleep? Try turning off your phone an hour before bed.
rows.id: Susah tidur? Coba matikan HP-mu satu jam sebelum tidur.

rows.en: We regret to inform you that the 7:15 train is cancelled.
rows.id: Dengan menyesal kami sampaikan bahwa kereta pukul 07.15 dibatalkan.

blocks.text: Good news for Indonesian speakers: the word **untuk** helps. *Berhenti merokok* = **stop smoking**. *Berhenti **untuk** merokok* = **stop to smoke**. So 'I stopped to smoke last year' (when you mean you quit) is a mistake: it says you stopped *in order to* smoke! Say **I stopped smoking last year.**

id.text: Kabar baik untuk penutur bahasa Indonesia: kata **untuk** membantu. *Berhenti merokok* = **stop smoking**. *Berhenti **untuk** merokok* = **stop to smoke**. Jadi 'I stopped to smoke last year' (kalau maksudmu sudah berhenti merokok) itu salah: artinya kamu berhenti *supaya bisa* merokok! Katakan **I stopped smoking last year.**

blocks.text:
Two honest notes.
- **try**: when something didn't work, native speakers often say both *I tried to call you* and *I tried calling you*. The difference is clear in two cases: **I'm trying to …** (an effort, it's hard: *I'm trying to concentrate*) and **Try + -ing** as advice (an experiment: *Try restarting it*).
- **regret** works like remember. **regret + -ing** = menyesal (sudah) melakukan: *I regret buying this phone.* **regret to** is mostly formal, in announcements and letters: *We regret to inform you that …* (Dengan menyesal kami beritahukan …).

id.text:
Dua catatan jujur.
- **try**: kalau sesuatu tidak berhasil, penutur asli sering memakai keduanya: *I tried to call you* dan *I tried calling you*. Bedanya jelas dalam dua kasus: **I'm trying to …** (usaha, karena sulit: *I'm trying to concentrate*) dan **Try + -ing** sebagai saran (percobaan: *Try restarting it*).
- **regret** mirip remember. **regret + -ing** = menyesal (sudah) melakukan: *I regret buying this phone.* **regret to** kebanyakan formal, di pengumuman dan surat: *We regret to inform you that …* (Dengan menyesal kami beritahukan …).

blocks.prompt: Please turn the music down. I'm trying ___ for my exam tomorrow.
blocks.explain: Studying with loud music is hard, and you're making an effort, so try + to: I'm trying to study. 'I'm trying studying' is not natural English: try + -ing is for an experiment (Try studying in the library).

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Please turn the music down. I'm trying ___ for my exam tomorrow.
id.explain: Belajar dengan musik keras itu sulit, dan kamu sedang berusaha, jadi try + to: I'm trying to study. 'I'm trying studying' bukan bahasa Inggris yang wajar: try + -ing untuk percobaan (Try studying in the library).

material.title: used to, be used to, get used to

id.title: used to, be used to, get used to

blocks.text:
You know **used to + base form** from B1: *I used to live in Bogor* = dulu (now it isn't true). Two expressions look almost the same, but the meaning is different:
- **be used to + -ing / noun** = **sudah terbiasa**: it's normal for you; it isn't difficult or strange any more. *I'm used to getting up at 5. She's used to the traffic.*
- **get used to + -ing / noun** = **mulai terbiasa / jadi terbiasa**: the change, step by step. *It took me a month to get used to working from home.*

Why -ing? In *be / get used to*, the word **to** is a **preposition** (a small linking word like *in, at, for*), just like in *I look forward to meeting you*. After a preposition comes a **noun** or an **-ing form**, never the base form. So: *I'm used to **waking** up early*, not 'I'm used to wake up early'.

id.text:
Kamu sudah kenal **used to + bentuk dasar** dari B1: *I used to live in Bogor* = dulu (sekarang tidak lagi). Ada dua ungkapan yang hampir sama bentuknya, tapi artinya berbeda:
- **be used to + -ing / kata benda** = **sudah terbiasa**: hal itu sudah biasa untukmu; tidak sulit atau aneh lagi. *I'm used to getting up at 5. She's used to the traffic.*
- **get used to + -ing / kata benda** = **mulai terbiasa / jadi terbiasa**: proses berubahnya, sedikit demi sedikit. *It took me a month to get used to working from home.*

Kenapa -ing? Dalam *be / get used to*, kata **to** adalah **preposisi** (kata penghubung kecil seperti *in, at, for*), sama seperti dalam *I look forward to meeting you*. Sesudah preposisi datang **kata benda** atau **bentuk -ing**, tidak pernah bentuk dasar. Jadi: *I'm used to **waking** up early*, bukan 'I'm used to wake up early'.

blocks.text: **be used to** and **get used to** work in **any tense**: *At first I **wasn't used to** the cold in Bandung. Don't worry, you'll **get used to** it. I've **got used to** the new office* (British; American English says *I've **gotten** used to*). But **used to + base form** is only for the past.

id.text: **be used to** dan **get used to** bisa dipakai di **semua tense** (bentuk waktu): *At first I **wasn't used to** the cold in Bandung. Don't worry, you'll **get used to** it. I've **got used to** the new office* (bahasa Inggris British; bahasa Inggris Amerika bilang *I've **gotten** used to*). Sedangkan **used to + bentuk dasar** hanya untuk masa lalu.

rows.en: I used to work at night, but now I have a day job.
rows.id: Dulu saya kerja malam, tapi sekarang saya kerja siang.

rows.en: I'm used to working at night.
Rina is getting used to her new job in Surabaya.
rows.id: Rina mulai terbiasa dengan pekerjaan barunya di Surabaya.
rows.note: get used to + noun = mulai terbiasa

id.note: get used to + kata benda = mulai terbiasa

rows.en: At first I wasn't used to the cold weather in Bandung.
rows.id: Awalnya saya belum terbiasa dengan udara dingin di Bandung.

rows.en: Don't worry, you'll soon get used to living alone.
rows.id: Tenang, nanti kamu akan cepat terbiasa tinggal sendiri.

id.note: masa depan: will get used to + -ing

blocks.text:
Indonesian trap: *biasa* and *terbiasa* are different.
- *Saya **biasa** bangun jam 5* (a habit now) = **I usually get up at 5.**
- *Dulu saya biasa bangun jam 5* (a habit in the past) = **I used to get up at 5.**
- *Saya sudah **terbiasa** bangun jam 5* (it isn't hard for me) = **I'm used to getting up at 5.**
The small words **am / is / are / was** (or **get**) and the **-ing** change the meaning completely.

id.text:
Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: *biasa* dan *terbiasa* itu berbeda.
- *Saya **biasa** bangun jam 5* (kebiasaan sekarang) = **I usually get up at 5.**
- *Dulu saya biasa bangun jam 5* (kebiasaan di masa lalu) = **I used to get up at 5.**
- *Saya sudah **terbiasa** bangun jam 5* (sudah tidak berat lagi untukku) = **I'm used to getting up at 5.**
Kata kecil **am / is / are / was** (atau **get**) dan **-ing** mengubah artinya sama sekali.

blocks.prompt: Pak Hasan has lived in Jakarta for twenty years. The traffic doesn't stress him any more: he ___ sitting in traffic.
blocks.explain: It's normal for him now (sudah terbiasa), so be used to + -ing: he is used to sitting in traffic. 'used to' alone would mean dulu, and 'uses to' doesn't exist.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Pak Hasan has lived in Jakarta for twenty years. The traffic doesn't stress him any more: he ___ sitting in traffic.
id.explain: Sekarang hal itu sudah biasa untuknya (sudah terbiasa), jadi be used to + -ing: he is used to sitting in traffic. 'used to' saja berarti dulu, dan 'uses to' tidak ada.

material.title: want someone to …, and make / let

id.title: want someone to …, serta make / let

blocks.text:
To say what you want **another person** to do, English uses **verb + object + to + base form**. The **object** is the person who receives the action: *me, you, him, her, us, them, Budi, my team*.
- **want / would like** + someone + to: *My boss wants me to lead the meeting. I'd like you to meet Sari.*
- **ask** (= meminta) + someone + to: *Rina asked me to check her CV.*
- **tell** (= menyuruh) + someone + to: *The doctor told him to rest.*
- **expect** (= mengharapkan, menuntut) + someone + to: *They expect us to reply within a day.*
- **need** + someone + to: *I need you to sign this form.*
For a negative, put **not** before to: *She told me **not to** worry.*

id.text:
Untuk mengatakan apa yang kamu ingin **orang lain** lakukan, bahasa Inggris memakai **kata kerja + objek + to + bentuk dasar**. **Objek** = orang yang menerima tindakan: *me, you, him, her, us, them, Budi, my team*.
- **want / would like** + seseorang + to: *My boss wants me to lead the meeting. I'd like you to meet Sari.*
- **ask** (= meminta) + seseorang + to: *Rina asked me to check her CV.*
- **tell** (= menyuruh) + seseorang + to: *The doctor told him to rest.*
- **expect** (= mengharapkan, menuntut) + seseorang + to: *They expect us to reply within a day.*
- **need** + seseorang + to: *I need you to sign this form.*
Untuk kalimat negatif, taruh **not** sebelum to: *She told me **not to** worry.*

rows.en: My boss wants me to lead the meeting.
rows.id: Bos saya ingin saya memimpin rapatnya.

rows.en: I'd like you to meet my colleague, Sari.

blocks.text: Indonesian trap: *Dia ingin **agar** saya datang* or *Dia mau saya datang*. Word by word, this becomes 'She wants **that I come**' or 'She wants **I come**'. English **want** doesn't take *that* + a sentence. Use the object form: **She wants me to come.** (me, not I; him, not he; us, not we; them, not they.) Also: **suggest** does **not** use this pattern ('He suggested me to go' ✗); remember suggest + -ing from B1.

id.text: Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: *Dia ingin **agar** saya datang* atau *Dia mau saya datang*. Kalau diterjemahkan kata per kata, jadinya 'She wants **that I come**' atau 'She wants **I come**'. Dalam bahasa Inggris, **want** tidak diikuti *that* + kalimat. Pakai bentuk objek: **She wants me to come.** (me, bukan I; him, bukan he; us, bukan we; them, bukan they.) Satu lagi: **suggest** **tidak** memakai pola ini ('He suggested me to go' ✗); ingat suggest + -ing dari B1.

blocks.text:
**make** and **let** use the same idea but **without to**.
- **make** someone **do** = membuat / memaksa (they have no choice): *My boss made me redo the slides.*
- **let** someone **do** = membiarkan / mengizinkan: *My parents let me study in Yogyakarta.*
'let her to go' and 'made me to stay' are mistakes. **allow** means the same as let, but **with to**: *My parents allowed me to study in Yogyakarta.*

id.text:
**make** dan **let** memakai ide yang sama tapi **tanpa to**.
- **make** seseorang **do** = membuat / memaksa (orangnya tidak punya pilihan): *My boss made me redo the slides.*
- **let** seseorang **do** = membiarkan / mengizinkan: *My parents let me study in Yogyakarta.*
'let her to go' dan 'made me to stay' itu salah. **allow** artinya sama dengan let, tapi **pakai to**: *My parents allowed me to study in Yogyakarta.*

blocks.prompt: Bu Ani is strict: she doesn't let her students ___ their phones in class.
blocks.explain: let + object + base form, without to: let her students use. After want / ask / tell you need to, but make and let never take to.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Bu Ani is strict: she doesn't let her students ___ their phones in class.
id.explain: let + objek + bentuk dasar, tanpa to: let her students use. Sesudah want / ask / tell perlu to, tapi make dan let tidak pernah memakai to.

id.intro: Hai! Kamu sudah tahu I enjoy swimming, I want to go dan I used to live in Bogor. Sekarang kenalan dengan kata kerja yang maknanya berubah dengan -ing atau to (I stopped smoking tidak sama dengan I stopped to smoke!), beda used to dan I'm used to + -ing, serta cara mengatakan apa yang kamu ingin orang lain lakukan. Pemanasan: apa hal yang awalnya sulit untukmu, tapi sekarang sudah biasa?
suggestedQuestions: Bagaimana cara mengingat beda 'stop smoking' dan 'stop to smoke'?
Apa beda 'I used to' dan 'I'm used to'?
Kenapa tidak boleh bilang 'She wants that I come'?
